dedupe_keys.name: digital twin of 50 km of the karlsruhe basel line near offenburg for four track upgrade planning 2021

description: This case documents how a digital twin of an operating main line was captured to plan its expansion. DB Netz AG is upgrading the heavily used Karlsruhe-Basel line to four tracks and partly renewing it; on the section between Appenweier and Lahr, which includes the planned 11 km Offenburg tunnel, the engineering firm Obermeyer needed an accurate as-built model for design with Building Information Modelling (BIM). In April 2021 tmc, the digitalisation company of the Plasser & Theurer group, surveyed 50 km of track with the EM100VT track inspection vehicle, which carries three 360-degree rotating laser scanners and two high-resolution colour cameras, in two days of runs at 60 km/h fitted into gaps in the regular timetable. The runs produced about 5 billion points and 62,826 colour images (about 100 million points and 1,250 images per kilometre), which tmc processed in about 11 weeks into a digital as-built model with an average absolute accuracy of 2 cm. Coverage is one 50 km corridor in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. The case is described in a vendor story that is free to read; the point cloud and model are not public. Outcome: Obermeyer received a complete digital twin for BIM planning, and the vendor reports that survey costs were below manual methods, with no track closures and no repeat surveys; no independent evaluation is published. The case shows design and capacity planning of rail infrastructure from a mobile-mapping digital twin, and complements the ProRail track geometry and railML records catalogued here.
